project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A twinning programme that pairs Hydrogen Valleys with cities wanting to decarbonise their hard-to-abate sectors with renewable hydrogen, ending in a roadmap per city.
A Hydrogen Valley is a region where hydrogen production, transport and use are combined in one ecosystem. Twinning works through mentor-mentee pairs. This is a coordination and support action: the project organises selection, cooperation and planning, not hydrogen research or infrastructure.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
The project is expected to carry out four tasks for twinning pairs; hydrogen for heating is out of scope.
- Organise a selection procedure, for example public calls for expressions of interest, to pick the most promising twinning pairs
- Develop and implement a tailor-made set of collaborative activities for each pair
- Deliver for each twinned city a detailed roadmap for integrating renewable hydrogen into its industrial decarbonisation
- Facilitate interaction between participating cities on shared challenges and solutions
Collaborative activities can cover feasibility assessments (technology, hydrogen sources, business cases, regulation, stakeholders), detailed implementation plans (funding, permitting, infrastructure needs, supply chains), environmental and socio-economic impact assessment, best-practice sharing, and education and training. The focus is on hard-to-abate or hard-to-electrify sectors: industry, heavy-duty and long-distance transport, aviation and maritime uses.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
More and more cities want hydrogen strategies for industry and transport but lack the expertise and tools that existing Hydrogen Valleys have.
The need originates with cities and their local and peri-urban industries and hard-to-abate sectors, which must decarbonise and improve air quality while staying competitive and socially cohesive.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A selection procedure, tailored activities per twinning pair, a detailed hydrogen roadmap per twinned city, and cross-city exchange.
- Calls or other procedures to select twinning pairs
- Tailor-made collaborative activities per pair
- One detailed roadmap per twinned city
- Activities connecting participating cities
- Clustering with other Cities Mission projects
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The project should contribute to hydrogen investment in and around cities, communities of practice, and synergies between the Cities Mission and the Clean Hydrogen Partnership.
- Investments in and deployment of hydrogen applications and infrastructure for hard-to-abate sectors in and around cities, reducing local air pollution and bringing growth and jobs
- Communities of practice linking cities, ports, industry, local and regional government, researchers and citizens
- Enhanced synergies between the Climate-Neutral and Smart Cities Mission and the Clean Hydrogen Partnership (the EU's public-private partnership on hydrogen)
The call sets no quantified targets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
Each twinned city leaves with a roadmap for the next steps, and the project feeds the Cities Mission and Hydrogen Valley platforms.
- Detailed roadmaps for integrating renewable hydrogen in industrial decarbonisation
- Optimal use of the Hydrogen Valley Platform and the Cities Mission Platform
- A Memorandum of Understanding with the Cities Mission Platform as soon as possible after the start, and clustering with other Cities Mission projects
The call does not require deployment during the project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
A single organisation may apply; there is no minimum or maximum consortium size, and one project is expected.
For a coordination and support action, a proposal may be submitted by one or more legal entities established in an EU Member State or a country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 12–13 · B — Coordination and Support Actions, Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 27–28 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-04, Overview of this call

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no required partner types; at least one twinned city should be one of the 112 Mission cities.
Geographical balance between participating authorities is encouraged, and mentees may come from enlargement countries such as the Western Balkans, Ukraine and Moldova. The twinned cities and Hydrogen Valleys are selected by the project and need not be consortium members. Beneficiaries must be established in an EU Member State or Associated Country.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 12 · B — Coordination and Support Actions

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call sets no budget split, but the work plan must include resources for cooperation with the Cities Mission Platform and for clustering.
Since the grant is a lump sum (a fixed amount paid against completed work packages), the consortium must allocate the amount to work packages and partners in a detailed budget table.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Specific conditions and Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
For a single-applicant proposal, that applicant is automatically the coordinator.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Consortium composition

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but a hydrogen twinning programme for cities is naturally led by a city network or hydrogen agency; TenneT TSO B.V. would not be a natural lead.
Any eligible entity in a Member State may lead a coordination and support action.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 12–13, 36 · B — Coordination and Support Actions; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
TenneT could also contribute expertise to the twinning activities of Dutch cities without being in the consortium.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes in principle: as a beneficiary TenneT could receive funding up to 100% of its eligible costs, built into a lump sum.
This topic is a coordination and support action (a project that networks, coordinates or supports others, without research work of its own), for which the maximum rate is 100% for all participants. The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 5 million for the single project. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT could advise twinned Dutch cities on the electricity-grid side of renewable hydrogen: connection capacity for electrolysers and timing of grid reinforcement.
This is our interpretation. Implementation plans must cover infrastructure requirements, and renewable hydrogen needs large electrolyser connections. TenneT could draw on its Onshore and Offshore Grid Investment Plans 2026, Target Grid 2045 and its regional Energy boards with DSOs and governments. Its role would be expert input, since the project's core is city twinning.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: No new technology is required: the project transfers expertise and builds roadmaps; research activities are outside a coordination and support action.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 14 · B — Eligible activities, Coordination and support actions

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Governance and cooperation models: mentor-mentee twinning, communities of practice and city roadmaps.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Planning and capacity building: feasibility assessments, implementation plans and roadmaps, not demonstration.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: No demonstration is required.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: The project must use the Hydrogen Valley Platform and the Cities Mission Platform and cluster with other Cities Mission projects.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer:
Cities are the users: they are selected through the project's procedure and receive tailored activities and a roadmap.
Communities of practice should bring in ports, industry, local and regional government, researchers and citizens.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Expected Outcome and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
One project of around EUR 5 million is expected, which is the whole topic budget.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 5 million; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount set from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages)
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 27–28 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-04, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The single rate for all participants is up to 100% of eligible costs, built into the lump sum.
- Co-financing conditions: none required by the call
For lump sum grants the funding rate is part of the method for fixing the amount and does not appear in the grant agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget table, which must still follow the normal cost-eligibility rules.
- Eligible costs: the detailed budget table must contain only costs that would be eligible under an actual-cost grant (personnel, subcontracting, purchases, other direct costs), because the lump sum must approximate the costs actually incurred
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are included in the lump sum calculation at the standard 25% flat rate of direct costs (excluding subcontracting)
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest; ineligible costs in the budget table can lead to a reduced grant, even late in the project
Payment depends on completing the work packages, not on proving the costs.
- Mandatory allocations: resources for cooperation with the Cities Mission Platform, synergies and clustering
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · G — Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 7 October 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 7 October 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 28 pages (the limit for lump sum coordination and support actions), with a detailed lump sum budget table
- Opening: 9 February 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 27–28 · Call HORIZON-MISS-2027-04, Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
- Conditions after the start: the Memorandum of Understanding with the Cities Mission Platform must be concluded as soon as possible after the starting date
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around March 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 28 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A and a detailed budget table, which is the basis for the lump sum
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Lump sum: the detailed budget table is mandatory and is used to fix the lump sum
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, pertinent objectives; quality of the coordination and support measures), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated by coverage of aspects not otherwise covered, then Excellence, then Impact, then gender balance and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: comments on the lump sum budget table are given to proposals invited to grant preparation and to those rejected for significant over- or underestimation of costs
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 24, 26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 28 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Mission-city participation, the Cities Mission Platform agreement and the exclusion of hydrogen for heating are specific to this topic.
- Conditional — Mission city: at least one twinned city should be one of the 112 Mission cities
- Conditional — Cities Mission Platform: a Memorandum of Understanding soon after the start, with resources for cooperation and clustering; grants are linked to the platform's action HORIZON-MISS-2021-CIT-02-03
- Conditional — scope: hydrogen for heating is out of scope
- Recommended: geographical balance; mentees from enlargement countries; use of the Hydrogen Valley Platform
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Missions · pp. 161–163 · HORIZON-MISS-2027-04-CIT-02, Specific conditions and Scope
